findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses status: String and two independent bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) so any combination of values is constructable, including impossible states like status=draft with is_sent=true or is_validated=true with status=invalid.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code cannot assume valid packet lifecycle; callers may observe or propagate logically impossible state, causing silent correctness bugs or unexpected branch execution.
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, and is_sent: bool with a single enum typestate (e.g., enum PacketStatus { Created, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }) so invalid combinations are unconstructable at compile time.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a boolean lifecycle flag that should be an enum or typestate. Booleans carry no domain semantics and allow ambiguous transitions (e.g., transitioning back from validated).
findings.failure_mode: Callers can flip is_validated in either direction without domain enforcement, enabling state regression (e.g., re-processing an already-validated packet).
findings.fix: Replace with a typestate enum or fold into the unified PacketStatus enum so transitions are explicit and one-way.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a boolean lifecycle flag. Independent of status: String, this creates dual representation of sent-state and allows the flags to diverge.
findings.failure_mode: item.status and item.is_sent can disagree (e.g., status=sent but is_sent=false), breaking any code that checks one but not the other.
findings.fix: Fold is_sent into the PacketStatus enum variant (e.g., PacketStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }) so sent-state and its timestamp are a single atomic value.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints. Packet IDs should carry length limits, format rules, or uniqueness invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid, duplicate, or oversized IDs are accepted at the type level, pushing validation burden to every call site instead of enforcing it at construction.
findings.fix: Create a PacketId newtype with a fallible constructor that enforces length/format constraints, and use it in PacketWorkflow.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates fields directly with string assignment (item.status = sent.to_string()) instead of returning a typed state transition. The function takes ownership and returns the same struct type, bypassing any type-level invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: No validation that the packet is in a pre-sent state before marking sent. Any PacketWorkflow instance can be marked sent regardless of prior lifecycle, enabling double-sent or out-of-order transitions.
findings.fix: Change to a pure function that takes the current typed state and returns the next typed state: fn mark_sent(state: PacketStatus) -> Result<PacketStatus, TransitionError> using enum pattern matching for valid transitions.

findings.problem: No functional core / imperative shell separation. PacketWorkflow and mark_sent mix data representation with state mutation in a single module with no clear boundary between inert domain data and action logic.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants cannot be tested independently of I/O side effects; refactoring or adding new state transitions requires changing the data type itself.
findings.fix: Define PacketStatus as an inert enum (Data layer). Implement mark_sent as a pure function in a Calculations module that takes PacketStatus and returns Result<PacketStatus, TransitionError>. Shell code handles I/O and persistence.

no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in PacketWorkflow construction or mark_sent
no allocation analysis for String allocations on id and status fields
no second-ring analysis for downstream consumers of PacketWorkflow
no command evidence (no cargo fmt/test/clippy run)
no test suite or behavior tests to verify state machine invariants
residual_risk: Review identified 6 BLOCKER findings. The crate has no type-level state enforcement, uses raw primitives for domain values, and lacks a functional core. No commands were run; all findings are from static analysis only. Without enum-based typestates the packet lifecycle is fully unenforced at compile time.
